title: Data Description
text:
The data for this report comes from the US Census Bureau and from the The National Historical Geographic Information System from the University Minnesota, which repackages data from the US Census Bureau for easier use.
Any data from the American Community Survey represents an average of the last five years of data collected for that measure.

Sources Used
U. S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates: Comparison Profiles 5-Year, 2020, accessed June 2, 2026, http://api.census.gov/data/2020/acs/acs5.
U. S. Census Bureau American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates: Comparison Profiles 5-Year, 2020, accessed June 2, 2026, http://api.census.gov/data/2010/acs/acs5.
U. S. Census Bureau Decennial Census: Redistricting Data (PL 94-171), 2020, accessed June 2, 2026, http://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/pl.
U. S. Census Bureau Decennial SF1, 2010, accessed June 2, 2026, http://api.census.gov/data/2010/dec/sf1.
U. S. Census Bureau Tn_od_main_JT00_2020, LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics, 8.3, 2020, accessed June 2, 2026, https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/.
U. S. Census Bureau 2020 TIGER/Line Shapefiles (Machine Readable Data Files), U.S. Department of Commerce, 2020, accessed June 2, 2026, https://www.census.gov/cgi-bin/geo/shapefiles/index.php.
IPUMS NHGIS, University of Minnesota, www.nhgis.org


Data Management
High level description: ACS and Census column labels were cleaned to standardize them and prepare them for analysis and place names were changed to a more readable form. The data was subset to only those counties in ETDD’s counties. Data was aggregated where needed to form Place-level and County-level data- in some cases this required combining place-level data for places that are in multiple counties (e.g. Oak Ridge).
Tiger files were used to get the area of each municipality and county. The area was converted into square miles and combined with the census data population to get population density. The data was subset to only those counties in ETDD’s counties.
IPUMS data was subset, the column names were changed, and changes from year to year were calculated and added to the data.
LODES data was combined at the county level and the crosswalk was used to add the correct label for each county.

Please note: this list is currently incomplete and will be updated at a later date

Demographic Characteristics

Population growth from 1970 to 2020;
population density
sex, race, and age
educational level of the adult population
housing characteristics in terms of age of the housing stock and type of tenure

Economic Characteristics

family income, household income, per capita income,
poverty status of families;

labor force by place of work and commuting patterns;

title: ETDD Census Data
text:
This report examines statistical data from U.S. Census materials with a focus on economic and demographic characteristics for the 16 counties that make up the East Tennessee Development District. It uses data from the U.S. Decennial Census and American Community Survey Five-year Estimates as its primary sources, with supplemental material from the National Historical Geographic Information System and the LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES). Please see the Data Description Tab for a detailed list of where the data comes from and a high-level description of any data management.




Data in Each Sub-Dashboard
Topics that will be discussed in the summary report for each county are:

Demographic Characteristics

Population growth from 1970 to 2020
population density
sex, race, and age
educational level of the adult population
housing characteristics in terms of age of the housing stock and type of tenure

Economic Characteristics:

family income, household income, and per capita income
poverty status of families
employment classification according to industry
labor force by place of work and commuting patterns









NoteHow to use this report




Hover over “Counties”, then click on the county you want information for
Click on the tab for the category of information you want
Click on the tab for the table and graph you want
Most graphs are interactive- if you hover your mouse over them you will notice controls like zooming in or out. You can hover over data points to get the exact numbers and category label (which are also in the corresponding table). You can click and drag to limit the graph to a smaller part of the overall data. On some graphs, if you click on the color boxes to the side you can show/hide some of the categories in the graph.
